name: The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2026-04-01.136.2) to agree with the amendments made to the bill in the Senate. Since this means the bill in its final form has now been agreed to in both the Senate and the House, it can now become law. ### What do these amendments do? According to the [supplementary explanatory memorandum](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22legislation%2Fems%2Fr7385_ems_1139314e-92c8-4b47-a1e1-88166a32b9dc%22;rec=0) (which is a document prepared by the Government, who introduced the bill and amendments): > *The purpose of these amendments ... is to ensure the Commonwealth Parole Board can continue to discharge its functions in circumstances where it is not appropriate that the Chair or Deputy Chair of the Board participate in making a decision or either is not available.* > > *[They] remove the ability of the Chair of the Commonwealth Parole Board (the Board) to request the Secretary of the Department to participate as a member of the Board in a meeting of the Board, or in making a decision without a meeting. It removes the ability for the Secretary to delegate this function to senior executive officers in the Department.* > > *The amendments instead allow the Chair to request a sessional member to participate in a meeting or in making a decision of the Board in the capacity of the Chair or the Deputy Chair in specified circumstances.* ### What does the bill do?
